new_finding.title: Publishable disk bytes and symlinks can evade Git-index-based dirty checks
new_finding.observed: require_clean_delivery_workspace compares published path membership but trusts git diff HEAD for byte integrity. Both assume-unchanged and skip-worktree hide a tracked site/app.js body change; the actual helper accepts it. With skip-worktree, replacing that tracked path with a symlink to a synthetic external file is also accepted. HEAD/runtime/data/registry need not change.
new_finding.impact_boundary: This is a post-validation source-integrity defect before production enrollment, not an empty-registry authorization bypass. The actual publisher copies the entire site tree. No generation, external data read, publication or real token mint occurred.
new_finding.probe_scope: Real synthetic Git repositories and the current actual helper; no monkeypatch of authorization or native validators. Only the Git index flags changed.
new_finding.recommendation: Read every published HEAD path through read_current_preimages to reject final/component symlinks, read its immutable HEAD regular blob and compare exact bytes directly. Keep inventory/unknown-file/known-seal checks; use Git dirty reporting only as an additional check.
